title: Queue under pressure
summary: Test technical truth, stable visual identities and whether animation explains backpressure.
originNote: Original fictional task for cross-model animation comparison. Skill workflows are separate layers of this one recipe; the benchmark shape awaits owner acceptance.

setup.instructions: Read fixtures/brief.md. If a skill layer is mounted at skill/, read skill/SKILL.md before planning; otherwise work from the brief alone. Kitchen supplies the same pinned toolchain (Node 22 or later, Python, a browser, FFmpeg and fonts) and compute profile to every compared model and layer. Before Ready, that toolchain must be pinned and smoked; this draft is not cookable.

turns.content: Read fixtures/brief.md and any mounted skill. Create Queue under pressure and deliver the specified movie, live player, source, contact sheet and evidence. Make routine creative decisions yourself and iterate from rendered evidence.

checks.description: Check delivery files, unchanged player, PNG signature, H.264/AAC, 1920 by 1080, 30fps, 720 frames, 24 seconds, complete decode, true peak at or below -0.1 dBTP and evidence structure. Check the pure queue state function at event boundaries, between events and out of order.

Can a viewer distinguish queue capacity from a busy worker? Does the visible film match the supplied trace, including blocked jobs? Can you explain backpressure after watching without reading the source? Inspect actual playback, audio, authorship and correspondence between evidence times and visible events.
